rationale: This is essentially assets-to-market / intangible-adjusted enterprise-value cheapness, a well-published anomaly family (Peters–Taylor intangible capital, asset-to-market value) and a close cousin of the archive's ProductiveRDCapitalValue and IntangibleBurdenEVYield, both of which already produced negative FF5 alphas despite positive FMB slopes.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archive's MarketBookGapKnowledgeCover (identical structure with `che` added to both numerator and the covering term), effectively splicing in the cash leg from LiquidKnowledgeValue rather than testing a new mechanism.

Pre-R&D earnings yield times a one-year margin-change term is a near-duplicate of the archive's RDEnabledCostEfficiencyValue (which uses the negative change in COGS/revenue, i.e. the gross-margin analogue of the same trend), and the margin-trend leg alone is the known profitability-trend anomaly.

This is the same "earnings yield amplified by R&D intensity" conditional already tested twice in the archive (RDAmplifiedBookValue, ValueWithRDCommitment, and the payout-scaled PayoutSupportedKnowledgeYield) with only a different denominator normalization, and it sits in direct tension with ExpensiveRDEarningsBurden's finding that high R&D-to-earnings burden predicts negatively.

This is a sign-flipped restatement of the archive's KnowledgeDeleveragingValue (both legs negated, same conditioning story and same knowledge-adjusted leverage-change construct), so it cannot deliver independent evidence.

Proximity-of-current-asset-productivity-to-own-five-year-peak is a genuinely distinct conditioning variable from the archive's volatility-based (DurableKnowledgeDemandValue) and change-based (CommercializingKnowledgeValue) productivity legs, the bounded [0,1] construction is well-behaved for a positive revenue/asset ratio, and the value-trap-avoidance rationale coherently matches the expected positive sign.
